subject: MAP & Evaluation: monthly TPM trajectory + commercial terms
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Burnham <iburnham@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: MAP & Evaluation: monthly TPM trajectory + commercial terms

Hi Irene,

Great to meet last week — thanks for the time. As discussed I put together an initial mutual action plan (MAP) and a suggested evaluation -> commit trajectory tied to monthly tokens (TPM) so we can align commercial terms to milestone progress. High level:

- 30-day evaluation (proof-of-concept) with token cap for the eval period
- Post-eval: initial committed minimum and month-by-month ramp targets to reach steady-state TPM
- Pricing: base per-token rate during eval, then tiered discounts tied to committed TPM bands and achieved ramp milestones

Attached: MAP_v1_Finexa.pdf (draft) with milestone dates and a sample pricing ladder. A few specific asks if you can review:

1) Does the proposed ramp (M1:10M, M2:25M, M3:50M, M4:75M, M5:100M) match Finexa’s expected production adoption curve?
2) Are you able to commit to a minimum contractual TPM after the eval (we proposed 50M/month starting month 3)?
3) Any procurement timing constraints we should factor into the target close date (we were thinking ~6 weeks post-eval to PO)?

If helpful I’m free for a 30-min sync next week to walk through the MAP and pricing.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v1_Finexa.pdf (PDF, 198KB)]
From: Irene Burnham <iburnham@finexa.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 11:02:00 -0500

Hi Soojin — thanks for the draft. Quick questions after skimming:

- The ramp you proposed looks sensible, but can we make the contractual commit smaller up front and accelerate discounts based on achieved TPM (not just committed)? We want flexibility during month-to-month adoption.
- How are overages billed if we exceed committed TPM during the ramp months?
- We have a data residency requirement for certain PII calls; does Redwood support region pinning for the evaluation?

Also, what would the pricing look like if we hit 120M TPM by month 4 vs your 100M target?

Can you share a redlined MAP and a clear pricing spreadsheet? I’ll loop procurement once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Irene Burnham
Head of Data & AI, Finexa
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: FW: MAP & Evaluation: pricing options

Internal — quick pricing note before we reply to Finexa:

- Consider moving the first formal commit to 25M TPM (month 2) with an attainment-based accelerator: if they exceed target in two consecutive months, they get bumped to the next discount band retroactively for that quarter.
- Proposed discount bands (after eval): 5% @ 25M, 10% @ 50M, 15% @ 100M, 22% @ 250M.
- Overage: bill at list price with a rolling credit if sustained overage > 120% for two months.

Dylan — can you model unit economics for the 25M starter commit vs 50M baseline? Laura — any procurement constraints on retroactive credits?

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP & Evaluation: monthly TPM trajectory + commercial terms

Hi Irene — thanks for the feedback. We took your flexibility ask into account and updated the MAP + pricing.

Key changes in attached MAP_v2_Finexa.pdf and redwood-pricing-v3.xlsx:
- Eval: 30 days with capped tokens for POC.
- Initial committed path (example):
  - Month 1 (post-eval ramp): 10M TPM (low-risk starter)
  - Month 2: 25M TPM (contractual minimum if you choose the starter commit)
  - Month 3: 50M TPM
  - Month 4: 75–100M TPM target (you can front-load to reach 100M if adoption supports it)
- Pricing approach: discount applied based on achieved TPM each month, with an attainment accelerator: if achieved TPM >= next band for 2 consecutive months, you move to that discount band and it is applied retroactively for the quarter.
- Discount bands (example): 5% at 25M, 12% at 50M, 18% at 100M, 25% at 250M.
- Overage policy: billed at list rate; sustained overage (>120% of commit for two consecutive months) triggers a credit/true-up conversation and optional commit increase.
- Data residency: we can pin inference to a US region for the eval and provide SOC2 artifacts for procurement.

Next steps we propose:
1) You review MAP_v2 and pricing spreadsheet.
2) Quick 30-min call to agree which starter commit option you prefer (25M vs 50M).
3) DocuSign route for the MAP + SOW + PO.

[Attachment: MAP_v2_Finexa.pdf (PDF, 255KB)]
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-v3.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)]

Look forward to your thoughts — happy to hop on a call Thursday or Friday.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP & Evaluation: monthly TPM trajectory + commercial terms

Soojin / Ben — thanks, this is clearer. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- We like the attainment accelerator but would prefer discounts to be earned on achieved TPM rather than strictly contractual commit (your revision already moves closer to that). Can we make the retroactive credit automatic (i.e., applied as a quarterly true-up) rather than on a case-by-case review?
- We want to accelerate ramp: can you give an example of pricing if we hit 120M TPM in month 4 (we expect a spike after a key product launch)?
- Procurement: we can likely sign the MAP + SOW as an interim document and then follow with a standard PO after the eval if the SOC2 artifacts look good. That shortens legal review.

If you can share a brief table with the unit economics under the two ramp scenarios (standard vs front-loaded to 120M month 4), I’ll take that to procurement.

Thanks,
Irene

- Discounts: attainment-based, applied retroactively at quarterly true-up. Bands: 5% @25M, 12% @50M, 18% @100M, 25% @250M.
- Overage: billed at list, auto true-up credit applied if sustained overage/attainment conditions met.
- Data residency & compliance: US region pinning for eval; SOC2 Type II report and architecture sketch attached to procurement packet.

Attachments included for procurement: MAP_v2_Finexa.pdf, redwood-pricing-v3.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf (SOC2 summary stub).
